description: Issue #839: a cross-depth duplicate in the NESTED-FIRST orientation. `dup` is declared inside `define outer` on line 2 and again at the top level on line 6, and `params.original_span` names the NESTED one — because "earlier" is a property of source order, not of depth. `spec/execution-model.md:86-87` is explicit that it is "a name an EARLIER declaration in the program already registered" that raises. Its mirror is `nested-duplicate-definition` (top-level first). Both orientations are needed: a two-pass registration that visited every top-level declaration before descending — a plausible "so forward references resolve" refactor — preserves the top-level-first orientation and INVERTS this one, flagging the line-2 declaration as the duplicate and naming line 6 as the original, so the learner stands on the earlier line and is told they already defined it later. Measured: that mutant passed all 890 fixtures and 3941 tests while only the top-level-first orientation was pinned.
